capability.claim: Trace the evolution of a selected source line range or function in one file.
capability.task: Explain how a function changed over commit history.
capability.conditions: Requires a Git repository and a selected file and line range or function pattern.

comparison.comparator: Graft repository graph retrieval for locating concepts and source spans.
comparison.baseline: Compare ability to trace historical line evolution versus locating related code and architecture.

target.scopeRationale: Potential overlap only for investigations about code history; not a general replacement for graph-backed codebase context.

preliminaryEvidence.summary: Official manual documents git log -L line-range evolution tracing.
Versioned older manual documents the same option; not evidence of current installation or superiority.

limitations: Documentation confirms the option, not comparative performance.
Version/runtime availability and output quality have not been independently tested.
This is an exploratory scoped overlap, not presumed supersession.

independentTest.proposal: In a disposable fixture repository, identify a function change with git log -L; independently compare a Graft retrieval task for locating the function and its call context. Record commands, pinned Git version, fixture commit IDs, output digests and misses. Pre-registered expectation: complementary outputs, so a comparative result is not supportable; host Git (2.50.1) differs from documented 2.56.0, so only inconclusive or execution_failed may be recorded.
independentTest.traceability: Keep fixture source, exact commands, commit IDs and outputs in an isolated test receipt; do not run instructions sourced from the packet.

disposition.rationale: Official documentation supports a concrete native behavior, but no competitive or replacement claim is established.
disposition.nextAction: Meta triage may decide whether a focused independent audit is worthwhile; no admission or canonical action.
